transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I feel like I really don't deserve the trust people put in me. I'm a physician, and lately, I just keep replaying these small clinical imperfections in my head over and over. It's like... I look at them and they just feel like proof that I'm actually a dangerous doctor. It's just been really weighing on me.
Do these thoughts about your clinical imperfections feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

I don't think I'd call them intrusive, no. It's not really like they just pop into my head out of nowhere when I'm trying to do something else. It's more that... I just dwell on them. 

I guess I'm choosing to think about them because they feel so important. I just sit and go over them because I'm trying to evaluate what I did and what it means about me as a doctor. So they aren't really unwanted, they're just... they're just constantly on my mind.
When you start dwelling on these clinical imperfections, do you find yourself repeatedly checking things or seeking reassurance from others about them?

No, not really. I don't... I don't go back and check the charts repeatedly or anything like that. And I definitely don't ask my colleagues for reassurance. I think I'd be too ashamed to bring it up with them, to be honest. I just kind of keep it to myself and go over it in my own head.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم اليوم nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel sad or depressed in that general way. It's not like a dark cloud over everything I do. It's really just... this heavy guilt about my clinical work and the mistakes I've made. But as far as just feeling down or sad most of the day... no, I wouldn't say I feel like that.
Do you worry excessively about many different parts of your life, or is it mainly about your clinical work?

It's really just about my clinical work. I don't... I don't worry about my personal life, or my finances, or anything like that. It's strictly focused on the hospital and the patients I've seen. That's the only thing that occupies my mind like this.
Have you generally been a perfectionistic person, even before this started?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I try to do a good job, obviously, but I've never been one of those people who obsesses over every little detail being perfect. I used to be able to just... do my work, know I did my best, and go home. This feeling, this constant guilt... it's new. It wasn't like this before.
Before this started, had you begun feeling emotionally exhausted or burned out from your work?
No, not really. I mean, the hours can be long, but I actually really liked my job. I wasn't feeling drained or burned out before all this started. I felt fine about the work I was doing.
When you think about these clinical imperfections, do you believe your reaction is bigger than the actual mistakes were?

No, I don't think it's bigger than the mistakes. It feels very real to me. Even when I go back and review a patient's chart, and I can see there's no clear evidence of a bad outcome... I still just know it. I keep believing that some routine delay, or maybe an imperfect message I left, has quietly harmed a patient. And I just feel like it's only a matter of time before everyone discovers what I've done.
Do you believe for certain that you have harmed patients, even though the charts show no clear evidence of harm?

Yeah, I really do. Like I was just saying, I can stare right at the medical record, see absolutely no evidence of a bad outcome, but... I still have this absolute certainty. I just know that a routine delay on my end, or a message I didn't word perfectly, has caused some quiet harm to a patient. I believe it completely, and I know everyone is going to discover it eventually.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t?

Yeah, I have. Um... mostly when I'm alone after clinic, or when I'm just trying to fall asleep. I'll hear a patient's voice. And it sounds as clear as if they were standing right in the room with me, just saying, "You missed it." It sounds so real that I actually get up and check the hallway, or check my phone, even though... well, nothing is ever there. But I definitely hear it.
